description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:206-209 — the DFS base case checks only names_match to terminate at a trust anchor:
  `for anchor in anchors { if pkix_path::names_match(&anchor.subject, &current_issuer) { return Ok(true); } }`

This means build_path can return a 'found' path where the last cert's issuer happens to match a trust anchor name, but the signature was NOT verified. This is intentional: the doc says 'Signatures are not verified here; that is the responsibility of the caller via validate_path.'

However, there is a subtle security issue: if the pool contains a cert issued by a rogue CA whose name matches a trust anchor, build_path will include it in the candidate path. The caller passes it to validate_path, which will then fail signature verification. This is not a security bug because validate_path is the authoritative checker.

BUT: build_path could also return a path terminating at the wrong anchor if there are two anchors with the same name (key rollover). It picks the first name-matching anchor without checking which one actually signed the chain. validate_path tries each anchor, so it will still work correctly.

No security bug. The doc contract is clear. Not filing.
title: pkix-path-builder dfs: anchor name-match without signature verification may accept wrong path
